desc: The life of a batch, from the data to the launch: brief it, plan it, check it, send it, and make sure it actually runs.

quests.d: Start a batch from what the data already proved, not from a request.
quests.why: The best batches start from what the data already proved. If you wait for someone to ask, you’re always one batch behind.
quests.brief: Using the PM’s best-performing-ads analysis, decide which angles to iterate, which to cut and why. Then turn it into the brief for the next batch.
quests.ex: Top ad by CPL: $18.7 with 124 leads. An ad at $71 with 4 leads isn’t a loser yet, it’s noise. Weigh winners by volume, not just cost.
rubric: I use CPL, CTR and hook rate, not just one
I weigh winners by lead volume
If an ad I expected isn’t in the report, I find out why before briefing
Every decision has a reason

reward.t: Reading hook rate and hold rate

quests.d: Number of ads, campaign details, resources and learnings.
quests.why: The batch brief is where performance learnings turn into the next ads. A thin brief gets you pretty ads that don’t move the KPI, and an outdated one gets you ads the client already changed their mind about.
quests.brief: Write the Batch Briefing for the next batch on one of your accounts, following the template checklist.
quests.ex: Objective: foundational assets. Key event: booked call. Few learnings yet because the funnel kept changing, so the founder-led videos stay, but they can’t be the only conversion driver.
quests.deliver: Link to the task or doc
rubric: I define the number of ads
I attached the PM’s best-performing-ads analysis
The brief reflects the latest positioning the client approved
I detail the campaign: key event and funnel stage
I list resources and last batch’s learnings

reward.t: The 5 brief mistakes I see most

quests.d: Propose batch dates that fit the Creative team before promising the client.
quests.why: A date you promise the client is a date the Creative team has to hit. If you commit before checking their load, someone else pays for it, and the client sees the slip.
quests.brief: Three requests land the same week: a refresh, a seasonal batch and a landing page. Propose dates for each, set the priority field, and write the message you’d send the client.
quests.ex: The Creative team can take one task or project per day, plus feedback on other briefs. Check with them before adding next-day tasks, and fill in priority on every ask.
rubric: I checked capacity before proposing dates
Each task has a priority
High-priority work goes first, low-priority work moves
The client message gives dates I can keep

quests.d: A batch with planted mistakes. Catch them all.
quests.why: You are the last filter before the client. Every mistake you catch here is one the client never sees.
quests.brief: This batch has planted mistakes. Select every piece you would not send to the client.

quests.d: Goal, angles, links by format and the right people tagged.
quests.why: The send message is the client’s first read of the strategy. It should explain why these ads exist, not just where to find them.
quests.brief: Write the message that sends a batch to the client: title, links by format, goal, angles being tested, feedback request and the right tags.
quests.ex: This batch includes the latest performance learnings, iterations on the formats and angles showing the strongest signals, and competitor research to guide the new executions. Could you leave feedback in Drive by Thursday?
rubric: I state the goal of the batch and the learnings behind it
I name the angles being tested
I ask for feedback in Drive with a date
I tag the Sr AM and the PM

quests.d: After approval: it’s live, it’s in the report, and the task is up to date.
quests.why: An approved batch that never gets tested is wasted work, and nobody learns from it. Approval isn’t the finish line, launch is.
quests.brief: Your batch was approved on Monday. Write the checklist you’ll run by Wednesday, and the update you’ll post in the internal channel.
quests.ex: A Creative strategist asked if last batch’s AI videos were ever tested. They weren’t in the report or in Ads Manager, so there was no learning to brief from.
rubric: I confirm the ads are live in Ads Manager
I confirm they show up in the report
I update the task with the latest client info
I tag the PM and the Creative strategist

quests.d: A cross-functional brief: right space, right template, all 12 sections.
quests.why: A Brief by AM blocks everything downstream. A vague one costs the cross-functional days of back-and-forth.
quests.brief: Write a Brief by AM for Funnels & CRM on an anonymized case. Create it in the right ClickUp space with the right template, and fill in all 12 sections.
quests.ex: Do not touch: Won and Disqualified stages, CAPI workflows, booking calendars, and leads abandoned manually by the setter.
rubric: It lives in the right space, built from the right template
Goal and Context are separate
Systems in scope and audience include volume
Do not touch is explicit
Done when is verifiable
